$comment: Every source the app's numbers and claims rest on, keyed by the id code cites as [ref:<id>]. usedBy lists the files that cite each entry; tests/references_test.ts keeps it and the tags in step. See AGENTS.md, 'Every threshold cites its source'.

1177-barns-somn-i-olika-aldrar.title: Barns sömn i olika åldrar

quotes.text: Så här mycket sover de flesta barn i olika åldrar: 0–3 månader: 14–18 timmar per dygn. 4–11 månader: 12–16 timmar per dygn. 1–2 år: 10–16 timmar per dygn. 3–5 år: 10-14 timmar per dygn.
De flesta barn i åldern 4–11 månader sover upp till 16 timmar per dygn. De sover 9–10 timmar på natten och 3–6 timmar på dagen.
När ett nyfött barn har varit vaket i en till två timmar på dagen brukar det vara dags att sova igen.
Efter ungefär 2 till 4 månader brukar barnet sova längre perioder på natten och vara vaken mer på dagen.

1177-barns-somn-i-olika-aldrar.supports: The Swedish picture beside the WHO range, the newborn's one-to-two-hour wake window, the 4–11 months night/day split, and the day–night rhythm between two and four months.
1177-barns-somn-i-olika-aldrar.note: Senast uppdaterad 2026-05-04. The page cites no source for its ranges.

fohm-2026-somnvanor.title: Främja goda sömnvanor bland barn och unga

quotes.text: Barn 4–11 månader: Sömnbehov 12–16 timmar, varav 3–6 timmar på dagen.

fohm-2026-somnvanor.supports: The same ranges as 1177, from the public health agency.

galland-2012.title: Normal sleep patterns in infants and children: a systematic review of observational studies

quotes.at: table 2, sleep duration in hours per 24 h, mean (mean ±1.96 SD)

quotes.text: Longest sleep period (h): 0–5 months 5.7 (1.8–9.6); 6–24 months 8.3 (3.0–13.7)
most children discontinue daytime napping between 3 and 5 years of age

galland-2012.supports: What children are observed to sleep at each age (OBSERVED_SLEEP), the sixteen-hour cap on one sleep (STALE_SLEEP_HOURS), night wakings being common, and the nap dropped between three and five.
galland-2012.note: The abstract gives 'all infants' as 12.8 (9.7–15.9) where table 2 gives 12.7 (9.0–16.3); the app uses the table's age rows only. There is no 3–4 years row.

grigg-damberger-2016.title: The Visual Scoring of Sleep in Infants 0 to 2 Months of Age

quotes.text: Sleep cycles in healthy infants at term typically last a mean of 50–60 min (range, 30–70 min)… At 43–48 w CA, sleep cycles average 60 min.

grigg-damberger-2016.supports: A nap under 45 minutes has not finished one sleep cycle; two hours or more has been through two (SHORT_NAP_MINUTES, LONG_NAP_MINUTES).

hirshkowitz-2015.title: National Sleep Foundation's sleep time duration recommendations: methodology and results summary

quotes.text: newborns (14–17 hours), infants (12–15 hours), toddlers (11–14 hours), preschoolers (10–13 hours)

hirshkowitz-2015.supports: The 14–17 hours for 0–3 months that the WHO adopted and the AASM declined to set.
hirshkowitz-2015.note: The NSF's wider 'may be appropriate' bands could not be checked against the paper, so the app does not use them; Galland et al. 2012's observed range stands in.

iglowstein-2003.title: Sleep duration from infancy to adolescence: reference values and generational trends

quotes.text: At 18 months of age, there was a significant change from 2 or more naps to only 1 nap per day.
At the age of 3 years, 50.4% of the children still napped.
9 months: total 13.9 ± 1.7 h, night 11.2 ± 1.0 h, day 2.8 ± 1.2 h

iglowstein-2003.supports: One nap from about 18 months, no wake-window suggestion from three, and the demo baby's night and day split.

jenni-lebourgeois-2006.title: Understanding sleep–wake behavior and sleep disorders in children: the value of a model

quotes.text: sleep pressure accumulates more slowly with increasing age… enabling children to be awake for consolidated periods during the day

jenni-lebourgeois-2006.supports: The physiology behind wake windows (the two-process model), and the reasoning that a short nap brings the next sleep sooner. The halfway adjustment for nap length is the app's own rule, not a measured one.

karitane-2016.title: Sleep Needs Guide for Infants 0 to 3 Years

quotes.text: 12–18 months: 4–6 hours; 18 months–3 years: 5–7 hours

karitane-2016.supports: Wake windows from the first birthday to three years (WAKE_WINDOWS).
karitane-2016.note: Updated May 2016. Superseded on Karitane's own site by the Flexible Daily Routine (karitane-flexible-routine), which stops at twelve months; the 2016 guide survives only as a copy on a third-party site. It is used because no service we found publishes a newer table past the first birthday.

karitane-flexible-routine.title: Flexible Daily Routine

quotes.text: 0–6 wk 1 hour; 6 wk–3 mo 1–1½ hours; 3–4½ mo 1½–2 hours; 4½–6 mo 2–2½ hours; 6–9 mo 2–3 hours; 9–12 mo 3 hours; 12 mo onwards: up for longer during the day

karitane-flexible-routine.supports: That Karitane's current guidance agrees with the 2016 guide to nine months and gives no table past twelve.
karitane-flexible-routine.note: Linked from https://karitane.com.au/newborn/infant-routines/. Undated; the upload path says January 2025.

kennaway-1992.title: Development of melatonin production in infants and the impact of prematurity

quotes.text: little evidence of rhythmic 6-sulfatoxymelatonin excretion before 9 to 12 weeks of age in full-term infants

kennaway-1992.supports: The newborn note that a day–night rhythm appears between two and four months.

paruthi-2016.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for Pediatric Populations: A Consensus Statement of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine

quotes.text: Infants 4 months to 12 months should sleep 12 to 16 hours per 24 hours (including naps) on a regular basis to promote optimal health.

Recommendations for infants younger than 4 months are not included due to the wide range of normal variation in duration and patterns of sleep, and insufficient evidence for associations with health outcomes.

paruthi-2016.supports: Agreement with the WHO from four months, the 10–13 hours carried to the sixth birthday (3–5 years), and why there is no AASM figure under four months.

rikshandboken-framja-god-somn.title: Främja god sömn

quotes.text: Spädbarn har sömncykler som är ungefär 50 minuter långa, lite kortare för de yngsta barnen, och lite längre för barn på ett år och äldre.
Barn mellan 1–5 år behöver 11–14 timmar sömn dagligen, med stora individuella skillnader.

rikshandboken-framja-god-somn.supports: The infant sleep cycle behind the short-nap threshold, in Swedish child health care's own words.

tresillian-3-to-5-months.title: Baby Awake Windows & Routines 3 to 5 Months

quotes.text: The average awake window for a 3 month old is 1.5 - 2 hours whereas an average awake window for a 5 month old is 2 - 3 hours.

tresillian-3-to-5-months.supports: Wake windows from twelve weeks to six months, turning at four months (WAKE_WINDOWS).
tresillian-3-to-5-months.note: The page shows no date; the year is when it was read.

tresillian-6-to-8-months.title: Baby Awake Windows & Routines 6 to 8 Months

quotes.text: 2 - 3 hours

tresillian-6-to-8-months.supports: Wake windows from six to nine months (WAKE_WINDOWS).
tresillian-6-to-8-months.note: The page shows no date; the year is when it was read.

tresillian-9-to-12-months.title: Baby Awake Windows & Routines 9 to 12 Months

quotes.text: around 2.5 - 3.5 hours
around 3 - 4 hours

tresillian-9-to-12-months.supports: Wake windows from nine months to the first birthday (WAKE_WINDOWS).
tresillian-9-to-12-months.note: The page shows no date; the year is when it was read.

tresillian-newborn-sleep.title: Newborn Sleep

quotes.text: Newborn to 6 week wake window: 1 to 2 hours
6 to 12 week wake window: 1 - 2.5 hours

tresillian-newborn-sleep.supports: Wake windows from birth to twelve weeks (WAKE_WINDOWS).
tresillian-newborn-sleep.note: The page shows no date; the year is when it was read.

who-2019-under5.title: Guidelines on physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep for children under 5 years of age

quotes.text: should have 14–17 hours (0–3 months of age) or 12–16 hours (4–11 months of age) of good quality sleep, including naps
should have 11–14 hours of good quality sleep, including naps, with regular sleep and wake-up times
should have 10–13 hours of good quality sleep, which may include a nap, with regular sleep and wake-up times
Strong recommendations, very low quality evidence

who-2019-under5.supports: The recommended hours of sleep per 24 hours, naps included, for each age band (SLEEP_RECOMMENDATIONS).
